```{r setup, include=FALSE}
## Import new ENST - ENST database

my_isoform_ppi_df <- read.delim("../data/transcript_specific_interactions_2.tsv", 
                          header = TRUE,
                          sep = "\t",
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

## Expand CellChat Database to Isoform Level

### Helper Functions

```{r}
# --- 1. Robust Parse Function ---
parse_complex <- function(name) {
  if (name %in% rownames(complex_db)) {
    # unlist and as.vector ensures we strip weird attributes
    subunits <- as.vector(na.omit(unlist(complex_db[name, ])))
    # trimws removes accidental spaces, and we filter empty strings
    subunits <- subunits[trimws(subunits) != ""]
    return(subunits)
  } else {
    return(character(0))
  }
}

expand_cellchat_with_complex_handling <- function(cellchat_row) {
  
  ligand_symbol <- cellchat_row$ligand
  receptor_symbol <- cellchat_row$receptor
  
  ligand_is_complex <- ligand_symbol %in% complex_ligands
  receptor_is_complex <- receptor_symbol %in% complex_receptors
  
  # --- HELPER: Get all isoforms (Unfiltered) ---
  get_isoforms_from_symbol <- function(gene_sym) {
    # Check Ligand column
    lig_ensts <- my_isoform_ppi_df %>% 
      filter(ligand_gene == gene_sym) %>% 
      pull(ligand_transcript)
    
    # Check Receptor column
    rec_ensts <- my_isoform_ppi_df %>% 
      filter(receptor_gene == gene_sym) %>% 
      pull(receptor_transcript)
    
    all_ensts <- unique(c(lig_ensts, rec_ensts))
    
    if (length(all_ensts) > 0) {
      return(all_ensts)
    } else {
      # Fallback to symbol if no isoforms found (prevents crash)
      return(gene_sym)
    }
  }

  # --- HELPER: Validate Interaction ---
  # Checks if ANY isoform on the left interacts with ANY isoform on the right
  validate_interaction <- function(ligand_isoforms, receptor_isoforms) {
    # subset PPI to relevant transcripts to speed up check
    relevant_ppi <- my_isoform_ppi_df %>%
      filter(
        (ligand_transcript %in% ligand_isoforms & receptor_transcript %in% receptor_isoforms) |
        (receptor_transcript %in% ligand_isoforms & ligand_transcript %in% receptor_isoforms)
      )
    return(nrow(relevant_ppi) > 0)
  }

  # =========================================================================
  # CASE 1: Simple -> Simple
  # =========================================================================
  if (!ligand_is_complex && !receptor_is_complex) {
    l_isoforms <- get_isoforms_from_symbol(ligand_symbol)
    r_isoforms <- get_isoforms_from_symbol(receptor_symbol)
    
    # Expand Grid
    combos <- expand.grid(L = l_isoforms, R = r_isoforms, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    
    # Filter valid interactions
    valid_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:nrow(combos), function(i) {
      l_curr <- combos$L[i]
      r_curr <- combos$R[i]
      
      if (validate_interaction(l_curr, r_curr)) {
        new_row <- cellchat_row
        new_row$ligand <- l_curr
        new_row$receptor <- r_curr
        new_row$interaction_name <- paste(ligand_symbol, receptor_symbol, sep = "_")
        new_row$interaction_name_2 <- paste(l_curr, r_curr, sep = " - ")
        return(new_row)
      } else {
        return(NULL)
      }
    }))
    
    return(list(interactions = valid_rows, complex_mapping = data.frame()))
  }

  # =========================================================================
  # CASE 2: Simple -> Complex
  # =========================================================================
  if (!ligand_is_complex && receptor_is_complex) {
    l_isoforms <- get_isoforms_from_symbol(ligand_symbol)
    
    # 1. Get subunits
    rec_subunits <- parse_complex(receptor_symbol)
    
    # 2. Get all isoforms for each subunit (No filtering yet!)
    rec_subunit_isoforms <- lapply(rec_subunits, get_isoforms_from_symbol)
    names(rec_subunit_isoforms) <- rec_subunits
    
    # 3. Expand all possible receptor complex combinations
    # This assumes independent assembly (we don't check intra-complex binding here)
    rec_combos <- expand.grid(rec_subunit_isoforms, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    
    # 4. Iterate and validate against Ligand
    interactions <- list()
    complex_map_list <- list()
    
    if(nrow(rec_combos) > 0) {
      for (i in 1:nrow(rec_combos)) {
        # Construct complex name
        curr_rec_sub_isos <- as.character(rec_combos[i, ])
        complex_name <- paste(curr_rec_sub_isos, collapse = "_")
        
        # Does this specific complex combination interact with ANY ligand isoform?
        # We pass the vector of subunits. If ANY subunit binds the ligand, it counts.
        if (validate_interaction(l_isoforms, curr_rec_sub_isos)) {
          
          # Now find WHICH ligand isoform specifically binds (could be multiple)
          for (l_iso in l_isoforms) {
            if (validate_interaction(l_iso, curr_rec_sub_isos)) {
              new_row <- cellchat_row
              new_row$ligand <- l_iso
              new_row$receptor <- complex_name
              new_row$interaction_name <- paste(ligand_symbol, receptor_symbol, sep = "_")
              new_row$interaction_name_2 <- paste(l_iso, complex_name, sep = " - ")
              interactions[[length(interactions) + 1]] <- new_row
            }
          }
          
          # Save Mapping
          map_row <- data.frame(complex_name = complex_name, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
          for (k in seq_along(curr_rec_sub_isos)) {
            map_row[[paste0("subunit_", k)]] <- curr_rec_sub_isos[k]
          }
          complex_map_list[[length(complex_map_list) + 1]] <- map_row
        }
      }
    }
    
    return(list(
      interactions = do.call(rbind, interactions), 
      complex_mapping = do.call(rbind, complex_map_list)
    ))
  }

  # =========================================================================
  # CASE 3: Complex -> Simple
  # =========================================================================
  if (ligand_is_complex && !receptor_is_complex) {
    r_isoforms <- get_isoforms_from_symbol(receptor_symbol)
    
    lig_subunits <- parse_complex(ligand_symbol)
    lig_subunit_isoforms <- lapply(lig_subunits, get_isoforms_from_symbol)
    lig_combos <- expand.grid(lig_subunit_isoforms, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    
    interactions <- list()
    complex_map_list <- list()
    
    if(nrow(lig_combos) > 0) {
      for (i in 1:nrow(lig_combos)) {
        curr_lig_sub_isos <- as.character(lig_combos[i, ])
        complex_name <- paste(curr_lig_sub_isos, collapse = "_")
        
        if (validate_interaction(curr_lig_sub_isos, r_isoforms)) {
          
          for (r_iso in r_isoforms) {
            if (validate_interaction(curr_lig_sub_isos, r_iso)) {
              new_row <- cellchat_row
              new_row$ligand <- complex_name
              new_row$receptor <- r_iso
              new_row$interaction_name <- paste(ligand_symbol, receptor_symbol, sep = "_")
              new_row$interaction_name_2 <- paste(complex_name, r_iso, sep = " - ")
              interactions[[length(interactions) + 1]] <- new_row
            }
          }
          
          map_row <- data.frame(complex_name = complex_name, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
          for (k in seq_along(curr_lig_sub_isos)) {
            map_row[[paste0("subunit_", k)]] <- curr_lig_sub_isos[k]
          }
          complex_map_list[[length(complex_map_list) + 1]] <- map_row
        }
      }
    }
    
    return(list(
      interactions = do.call(rbind, interactions), 
      complex_mapping = do.call(rbind, complex_map_list)
    ))
  }

  # =========================================================================
  # CASE 4: Complex -> Complex
  # =========================================================================
  if (ligand_is_complex && receptor_is_complex) {
    # 1. Expand Ligand
    lig_subunits <- parse_complex(ligand_symbol)
    lig_subunit_isoforms <- lapply(lig_subunits, get_isoforms_from_symbol)
    lig_combos <- expand.grid(lig_subunit_isoforms, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    
    # 2. Expand Receptor
    rec_subunits <- parse_complex(receptor_symbol)
    rec_subunit_isoforms <- lapply(rec_subunits, get_isoforms_from_symbol)
    rec_combos <- expand.grid(rec_subunit_isoforms, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    
    interactions <- list()
    complex_map_list <- list()
    
    # Loop over Ligand Combos
    if(nrow(lig_combos) > 0 && nrow(rec_combos) > 0) {
      for (i in 1:nrow(lig_combos)) {
        curr_lig_sub_isos <- as.character(lig_combos[i, ])
        l_complex_name <- paste(curr_lig_sub_isos, collapse = "_")
        
        # Loop over Receptor Combos
        for (j in 1:nrow(rec_combos)) {
          curr_rec_sub_isos <- as.character(rec_combos[j, ])
          r_complex_name <- paste(curr_rec_sub_isos, collapse = "_")
          
          # Check if ANY piece of Ligand Complex binds ANY piece of Receptor Complex
          if (validate_interaction(curr_lig_sub_isos, curr_rec_sub_isos)) {
            new_row <- cellchat_row
            new_row$ligand <- l_complex_name
            new_row$receptor <- r_complex_name
            new_row$interaction_name <- paste(ligand_symbol, receptor_symbol, sep = "_")
            new_row$interaction_name_2 <- paste(l_complex_name, r_complex_name, sep = " - ")
            interactions[[length(interactions) + 1]] <- new_row
            
            # Save Mapping (Ligand)
            l_map <- data.frame(complex_name = l_complex_name, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
            for (k in seq_along(curr_lig_sub_isos)) l_map[[paste0("subunit_", k)]] <- curr_lig_sub_isos[k]
            complex_map_list[[length(complex_map_list) + 1]] <- l_map
            
            # Save Mapping (Receptor)
            r_map <- data.frame(complex_name = r_complex_name, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
            for (k in seq_along(curr_rec_sub_isos)) r_map[[paste0("subunit_", k)]] <- curr_rec_sub_isos[k]
            complex_map_list[[length(complex_map_list) + 1]] <- r_map
          }
        }
      }
    }
    
    return(list(
      interactions = do.call(rbind, interactions), 
      complex_mapping = unique(do.call(rbind, complex_map_list))
    ))
  }
}
```

## Apply Expansion

```{r}
# Load the base CellChat DB
db.human <- CellChatDB.human

# --- !! IMPORTANT: Create 'complex_db' !! ---
# Your new function depends on this object.
# We will create it from the standard CellChat 'complex' data frame.
complex_db <- db.human[["complex"]]

# *** This is the most critical line ***
all_complex_names <- rownames(complex_db)

complex_ligands <- unique(db.human$interaction$ligand[db.human$interaction$ligand %in% all_complex_names])
complex_receptors <- unique(db.human$interaction$receptor[db.human$interaction$receptor %in% all_complex_names])
```

Execute the expansion

```{r}
# --- 1. Get all genes you have isoform data for ---
genes_in_my_ppi <- unique(c(my_isoform_ppi_df$ligand_gene, 
                            my_isoform_ppi_df$receptor_gene))

# --- 2. Get the base gene-level interactions ---
base_interactions <- db.human$interaction

# --- 3. Filter the base interactions (HIGHLY RECOMMENDED) ---
# This filters the ~2500 CellChat interactions down to only those
# where at least one partner is in your PPI file.
# Note: We must also check subunits of complexes!
complex_subunits <- unique(c(db.human$complex$subunit_1, db.human$complex$subunit_2, 
                             db.human$complex$subunit_3, db.human$complex$subunit_4, 
                             db.human$complex$subunit_5))
complex_subunits_in_ppi <- complex_subunits[complex_subunits %in% genes_in_my_ppi]

# Keep rows where:
# 1. The simple ligand is in your PPI
# 2. The simple receptor is in your PPI
# 3. The complex ligand has subunits in your PPI
# 4. The complex receptor has subunits in your PPI
filtered_interactions <- base_interactions %>%
  filter(
    (ligand %in% genes_in_my_ppi) |
    (receptor %in% genes_in_my_ppi) |
    (ligand %in% complex_ligands & ligand %in% db.human$complex$complex_name[db.human$complex$complex_name %in% complex_subunits_in_ppi]) |
    (receptor %in% complex_receptors & receptor %in% db.human$complex$complex_name[db.human$complex$complex_name %in% complex_subunits_in_ppi])
  )
  
cat("Total base interactions:", nrow(base_interactions), "\n")
cat("Filtered interactions to process:", nrow(filtered_interactions), "\n")


# --- 4. Apply your function to each filtered row ---
# This will be slow if 'filtered_interactions' is large
cat("Expanding interactions... This may take several minutes.\n")

# Create a list of rows
interaction_list <- split(filtered_interactions, seq(nrow(filtered_interactions)))

# Apply the function
results_list <- lapply(interaction_list, expand_cellchat_with_complex_handling)

cat("Expansion complete.\n")
```

## New complex table

```{r}
# --- 1. Combine all 'interactions' data frames ---
isoform_interactions <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(results_list, `[[`, "interactions"))

# --- 2. Combine all 'complex_mapping' data frames ---
isoform_complexes <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(results_list, `[[`, "complex_mapping"))

# --- 3. Clean up the new complex table ---
# Ensure it has the correct columns and no duplicates
if(nrow(isoform_complexes) > 0) {
  isoform_complexes_final <- isoform_complexes %>%
    distinct(complex_name, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    # Ensure it has the same 5 subunit columns as the original
    # (Your function already does this, but this is a safeguard)
    mutate(
      subunit_1 = if("subunit_1" %in% names(.)) subunit_1 else NA_character_,
      subunit_2 = if("subunit_2" %in% names(.)) subunit_2 else NA_character_,
      subunit_3 = if("subunit_3" %in% names(.)) subunit_3 else NA_character_,
      subunit_4 = if("subunit_4" %in% names(.)) subunit_4 else NA_character_,
      subunit_5 = if("subunit_5" %in% names(.)) subunit_5 else NA_character_
    ) %>%
    select(complex_name, subunit_1, subunit_2, subunit_3, subunit_4, subunit_5)
} else {
  # Create an empty but correctly structured data frame if no complexes were found
  isoform_complexes_final <- data.frame(
    complex_name = character(), subunit_1 = character(), subunit_2 = character(),
    subunit_3 = character(), subunit_4 = character(), subunit_5 = character()
  )
}

rownames(isoform_complexes_final) <- isoform_complexes_final$complex_name
isoform_complexes_final$complex_name <- NULL

# --- 4. Create your final database object ---
myIsoformCellChatDB <- list(
  interaction = isoform_interactions,
  complex = isoform_complexes_final,
  cofactor = db.human$cofactor, # We re-use the original cofactor
  geneInfo = db.human$geneInfo  # We re-use the original geneInfo
)

cat("New isoform-level database 'myIsoformCellChatDB' is built.\n")
print(paste("Total isoform interactions:", nrow(myIsoformCellChatDB$interaction)))
print(paste("Total isoform complexes:", nrow(myIsoformCellChatDB$complex)))
```

## Adding geneInfo table

```{r}

# --- 1. Extract and Combine Mappings ---

# Create a two-column map for ligands: Transcript -> Gene
ligand_map <- data.frame(
  Transcript = my_isoform_ppi_df$ligand_transcript,
  Gene = my_isoform_ppi_df$ligand_gene,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Create a two-column map for receptors: Transcript -> Gene
receptor_map <- data.frame(
  Transcript = my_isoform_ppi_df$receptor_transcript,
  Gene = my_isoform_ppi_df$receptor_gene,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Stack the two maps on top of each other
combined_map <- rbind(ligand_map, receptor_map)

# --- 2. De-duplicate and Format ---

# Get only the unique transcript-to-gene pairs
new_geneInfo <- unique(combined_map)

# Rename the columns exactly as you requested
colnames(new_geneInfo) <- c("Symbol", "gene.symbol")

# Remove any potential NA/empty transcript IDs
new_geneInfo <- new_geneInfo[!is.na(new_geneInfo$Symbol) & new_geneInfo$Symbol != "", ]

# Set the row names to be the transcript IDs (the 'Symbol' column)
# This is standard practice for CellChatDB objects and good for lookups
rownames(new_geneInfo) <- new_geneInfo$Symbol

# --- 4. Replace the old $geneInfo table ---
myIsoformCellChatDB$geneInfo <- new_geneInfo

# --- 5. (Optional) Check the result ---
cat("Successfully updated $geneInfo. Here's the new structure:\n")
print(head(myIsoformCellChatDB$geneInfo))
```

## Tricky: How to handle cofactors

```{r}
# Get all genes from the cofactor table
cofactor_genes <- db.human$cofactor %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unique()

genes_to_pool <- cofactor_genes[!is.na(cofactor_genes) & cofactor_genes != ""]

cat("Found", length(genes_to_pool), "unique gene symbols in the cofactor table.\n")

# EXTRA: Add cofactor symbols to geneInfo
# Get the names of the new rows we added
new_feature_names <- genes_to_pool

# Create a new data.frame for these features
new_geneInfo_rows <- data.frame(
  Symbol = new_feature_names,
  gene.symbol = new_feature_names,
  row.names = new_feature_names
)

# Add these new rows to your modified database's geneInfo
myIsoformCellChatDB[["geneInfo"]] <- rbind(myIsoformCellChatDB[["geneInfo"]], new_geneInfo_rows)

print("Successfully updated myIsoformCellChatDB[['geneInfo']] with pooled feature names.")
```

Create a hybrid object that includes transcript counts + cofactor gene counts

```{r}
# Get the counts matrix (aggregation should be on raw counts)
counts_matrix <- assay(sce_pc, "X")


# Connect to the Ensembl BioMart
ensembl_mart <- useMart(biomart = "ENSEMBL_MART_ENSEMBL",
                        dataset = "hsapiens_gene_ensembl",
                        host = "https://useast.ensembl.org")

# Get the transcript mappings for ALL your cofactor genes in one query
cofactor_genes <- db.human$cofactor %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unique()

genes_to_pool <- cofactor_genes[!is.na(cofactor_genes) & cofactor_genes != ""]

tx_map <- getBM(attributes = c('ensembl_transcript_id', 'hgnc_symbol'),
                filters = 'hgnc_symbol',
                values = genes_to_pool,
                mart = ensembl_mart)

print(paste("Found", nrow(tx_map), "transcript-to-gene mappings."))

# List to store the new, pooled expression vectors
pooled_rows <- list()

print("Starting aggregation...")
for (gene in genes_to_pool) {
  
  # 1. Find all transcripts (ENST IDs) for this gene *from our BioMart map*
  tx_for_gene <- tx_map$ensembl_transcript_id[tx_map$hgnc_symbol == gene]
  
  # 2. Find which of these transcripts are actually in your sce object
  tx_in_sce <- intersect(tx_for_gene, rownames(counts_matrix))
  
  if (length(tx_in_sce) > 0) {
    # 3. Subset the counts matrix for these transcripts
    # drop=FALSE ensures it stays a matrix even if only 1 tx is found
    tx_counts <- counts_matrix[tx_in_sce, , drop = FALSE]
    
    # 4. Aggregate by summing the columns (colSums)
    if (nrow(tx_counts) > 1) {
      pooled_expression <- colSums(tx_counts)
    } else {
      pooled_expression <- tx_counts[1, ] # Just take the single row
    }
    
    # 5. Store the new pooled vector
    pooled_rows[[gene]] <- pooled_expression
    print(paste("Successfully pooled", length(tx_in_sce), "transcripts for:", gene))
    
  } else {
    warning(paste("No transcripts for", gene, "found in sce object. Skipping."))
  }
}

sce_modified <- sce_pc_loc

# --- Combine and Update sce object (No change from before) ---
if (length(pooled_rows) > 0) {
  
  # 1. Create the matrix of new pooled rows
  new_rows_matrix <- do.call(rbind, pooled_rows)
  if (is(counts_matrix, "sparseMatrix")) {
    new_rows_matrix <- as(new_rows_matrix, "sparseMatrix")
  }

  # 2. IMPORTANT: Remove normalized assays from the *original* object first.
  # rbind will fail or produce NAs if these assays don't exist in both objects.
  if ("log1p" %in% assayNames(sce_modified)) {
    assays(sce_modified)[["log1p"]] <- NULL
  }
  if ("norm" %in% assayNames(sce_modified)) {
    assays(sce_modified)[["norm"]] <- NULL
  }
  print("Removed 'log1p' and 'norm' assays from original object before combining.")

  # 3. Create a new, temporary SingleCellExperiment object for the pooled rows
  # It MUST have the same colData and assay name ("X") to be compatible
  sce_new_rows <- SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(X = new_rows_matrix), # Must match the assay name 'X'
    colData = colData(sce_modified)      # Must include colData for rbind
  )

  # 4. Combine the original sce and the new rows object
  print(paste("Original sce features:", nrow(sce_modified)))
  print(paste("New pooled features:", nrow(sce_new_rows)))
  
  sce_combined <- rbind(sce_modified, sce_new_rows)

  # 5. Update our main 'sce_modified' variable to be this new combined object
  sce_modified <- sce_combined
  
  print(paste("New combined sce features:", nrow(sce_modified)))
  print("Successfully added pooled cofactor rows to sce object.")
  print("WARNING: You MUST re-normalize the 'sce_modified' object's 'X' assay.")
  
} else {
  print("No cofactor genes were found or pooled. 'sce' object is unchanged.")
}


print(sce_modified)
```
